classifications.item_title: Claude Code settings.local.json Secrets: 17 months of exposure on GitHub, & Docker Hub

kb_matches.rationale: Agent tooling persisted credentials/secrets to a file that was then publicly exposed, an agent-driven data exfiltration/exposure vector.
Agent's 'don't ask again' permission persistence writes secrets into config files beyond what users intended.
Agent-written artifacts containing sensitive data were not visible or audited by users.

classifications.evidence_quote: 31,088 distinct secrets in Claude Code's .claude/settings.local.json on public GitHub
classifications.recommended_action: Add this AIID incident (1846) as a real-world example to D2 and G5 on coding agents persisting secrets in local permission files that get committed publicly.

classifications.item_title: Coding Agents Copy Your Secrets to a Hidden File. Thousands Are on GitHub

kb_matches.rationale: Same incident: agents copy secrets into hidden files that end up on public GitHub.
Agent behaviour exceeded what users expected when approving commands.

classifications.evidence_quote: Coding Agents Copy Your Secrets to a Hidden File. Thousands Are on GitHub
classifications.recommended_action: Cite as a corroborating source for the incident 1846 update to D2 and G5; note vendor response.
